boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Reed study environments, from open library seating to reservable media-production rooms.

cards.title: Hauser Library Open Seating
cards.subtitle: Library main building
cards.notes: Bring your materials to any unreserved library table, desk, carrel, or comfortable seat; wireless access reaches most of the building.
cards.short_summary: Flexible open seating surrounded by Reed’s print collection and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that study desks, carrels, and comfortable seating are distributed throughout the library, and that wireless access is available throughout most of the building.
cards.access_notes: All seating except assigned thesis desks is open to the Reed community; do not reserve or leave belongings at open desks.

cards.title: South Stacks Collaborative Work Area
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, south end of South Stacks
cards.notes: Use the first-come collaborative area when your work needs a shared surface and whiteboards; bring a group or spread out a project.
cards.short_summary: A library collaboration zone with desks and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed Library identifies an open collaborative work area at the south end of South Stacks that is first come, first served; its map lists whiteboards and desks.
cards.source_title: Thesis Desks, Group Study Rooms, & Lockers — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: First come, first served; the library map identifies the collaborative space on LL1.

cards.title: Pollock Room
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, main level
cards.notes: Set up near current newspapers and magazines when you want a reading-focused pause between research tasks; check the library map for location.
cards.short_summary: A main-level library room alongside current periodicals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reed Library map lists the Pollock Room on the main level with current newspapers and magazines.
cards.source_title: Library Maps & Call Number Locations — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s main level; consult current library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Hauser Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library, level 2
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room in advance for a focused two-hour session; choose this option when your project needs a contained shared room.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms for Reed community group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed Library offers four group study rooms for Reed students, faculty, and staff; reservations can be from 30 minutes to two hours, up to two hours per day.
cards.source_title: Thesis Desks, Group Study Rooms, & Lockers — Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reservation only for Reed students, faculty, and staff; only one room may be booked at a time.

cards.title: Language Lab (L033)
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library LL1, inside the IMC
cards.notes: Practice a target language, use language-learning resources, or attend drop-in tutoring; confirm the current schedule before heading to L033.
cards.short_summary: A staffed language-learning room with resources and tutoring.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies the Language Lab as a multi-purpose space in room L033 on LL1 of Hauser Library, supporting language learning with resources and tutoring.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular IMC hours, with some extended evening hours; it may be reserved for classes or language-related activities.

cards.title: Instructional Media Center (L32)
cards.subtitle: Hauser Library LL1
cards.notes: Use the IMC when your coursework benefits from media resources or a computer-oriented setting; ask the desk about equipment and current access.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level media and computer resource facility with study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the IMC as a multimedia, audiovisual, and computer resource facility in L32; the library hours page identifies IMC study-space access.
cards.access_notes: Located on lower level one of the non-library part of the building; the IMC and Language Lab are listed as closed for summer break.

cards.entity_name: PARC Room 327: AV Recording & Editing Workroom
cards.title: PARC Room 327
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Reserve this room for course-related audio or video editing and recording; plan a concise two-hour block and use it for production rather than Zoom.
cards.short_summary: A reservable production workroom for audio and video coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says PARC Room 327 supports audio/video recording and editing, gives priority to course and assignment use, and uses first-come reservations.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reserve in two-hour blocks; academic purposes receive priority, and the room is not for Zoom meetings.

cards.title: PARC Room 330
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Book Room 330 to rehearse a presentation or coordinate media-heavy group work; its monitor, hookups, and whiteboard support structured sessions.
cards.short_summary: A reservable 12-seat workroom for presentations and group media work.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists Room 330 as a presentation and conference workroom with an LCD monitor, iMac and laptop hookups, and a whiteboard; it seats 12.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Reservations are first come, first served in two-hour blocks; academic purposes receive priority.

cards.entity_name: PARC Room 329: Video Viewing & MIDI Workroom
cards.title: PARC Room 329
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Choose this room for independent video viewing or MIDI composition work; its separate stations and headphones suit projects needing focused media playback.
cards.short_summary: A specialized room for video viewing and MIDI composition.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes PARC Room 329 as a video viewing and MIDI workroom with three independent iMac and MIDI-keyboard workstations, plus headphones.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Use is oriented to the room’s video-viewing and composition workstations; confirm current PARC access before visiting.

cards.title: PARC Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Performing Arts Resource Center
cards.notes: Work on a digital assignment at one of the lab’s iMacs, then use the printer, copier/scanner, or large-format flatbed scanner as needed.
cards.short_summary: A computer-based workspace with scanning and printing tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists the PARC Computer Lab as having fourteen iMacs, a Xerox printer and copier/scanner, a large-format flatbed scanner, and a library catalog workstation.
cards.source_title: Rooms — Performing Arts Resource Center, Reed Library
cards.access_notes: Check current Performing Arts Resource Center hours and access before planning computer or scanner use.
